name: Abū ʿUthmān ʿAmr ibn Baḥr ibn Maḥbūb al-Jāḥiẓ
summary: The great prose writer of Basra, Muʿtazilī and pupil of al-Naẓẓām, author of al-Bayān wa-l-tabyīn and al-Ḥayawān; Ibn al-Anbārī counts him among the masters of letters for his eloquence.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls al-Jāḥiẓ learned in letters, eloquent and articulate, an author in many branches and one of the leading Muʿtazilīs, a pupil of Abū Isḥāq al-Naẓẓām. His nephew Yamūt ibn al-Muzarraʿ is the source of much of the entry: that his grandfather was black and a camel-driver of the Kināna, and stories of his wit.
He died in Basra in 255/869. His books, above all al-Bayān wa-l-tabyīn and al-Ḥayawān, are the classic Arabic prose of the third/ninth century.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 254–259
